description: Flatten a width×height rectangle of terrain at (x,y) to a uniform height. Prerequisite: you are the lot owner (handler-side; server-side BuildBuyRoommate+). Effect: terrain heightmap at those tiles converges to the reference height (floor tiles that span a gradient get normalized). Observable via query-architecture at the affected tiles (floor presence/absence changes if slope leveled). Cost: flattening is generally free; server may reject outside the buildable area. Denial silent (OQ-8). Wire: VMNetArchitectureCmd { Commands: [{ Type: TERRAIN_FLATTEN, level, x, y, x2=width, y2=height }] }.
common_mistakes: Flatten baselines to the anchor tile's height; choose anchor carefully.
perception_hints: Am I the owner? perception.lot.owner_is_me — architecture ops are owner-only
Your position (to anchor where to build): perception.avatar.position.x, .y (tile coords — arch ops accept tile coords directly, unlike walk-to)
Walls/floors are NOT exposed in perception — use query-architecture (test helper) if you need pre/post state
refuse_conditions: caller is not lot owner → returns ok:false with 'caller is not lot owner (owner_id=..., me=...)'
required tile coords (x, y) missing → returns ok:false with '<verb> requires x, y ...'
width/height/length <= 0 where specified → returns ok:false with specific bounds error
